hero.headline: Federal judge blocks Trump's Kennedy Center closure and orders name removal
hero.body:
A federal judge has ordered the removal of Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, ruling that the Washington DC venue cannot be renamed without an act of Congress.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper directed the Trump administration to remove all physical signage bearing Trump's name and eliminate any references to a "Trump Kennedy Center" from official materials within 14 days. In his 94-page decision, the judge wrote that it was "crystal clear" the arts complex was named for the late President John F. Kennedy.

The ruling also blocks the Kennedy Center from closing for two years of planned renovations. The judge prevented the center from winding down programming and shutting down operations as the Trump administration had announced.

The decision came after Trump sought to add his name to the facility. The judge determined that only Congress has the authority to change the center's name, making the board's decision to rename it unlawful. The Kennedy Center was established as a federal memorial to President Kennedy, and that designation cannot be altered without congressional action.

Kennedy family members celebrated the ruling. Maria Shriver, JFK's niece, called it "an appropriate birthday present on my uncle's birthday." She noted that the judge found both Trump and the Kennedy Center Board had acted unlawfully. Kerry Kennedy, daughter of Robert F. Kennedy, wrote: "What a great way to celebrate you on your birthday, Uncle Jack!" Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who serves as Trump's health secretary, made no immediate comment.

Trump responded with a lengthy statement posted on social media hours after announcing he was entering the White House Situation Room regarding Iran. He attacked the judge, noting that Cooper had been nominated to the bench by Barack Obama. Trump also expressed anger at the 14-day deadline to remove his name from the Kennedy Center's facade and website.

Trump wrote that his handpicked board members "unanimously voted to add the name 'TRUMP' onto the former Kennedy Center," but the judge ruled they lacked the authority to do so. Trump said he was instructing the Department of Commerce to work with Congress on transferring the Kennedy Center back to legislative control, stating: "I have instructed the Department of Commerce to make all necessary arrangements with Congress to allow a full and complete transfer of this Institution, giving them the responsibility for its Operation, Maintenance, and Management."

The Kennedy Center has served as Washington's primary performing arts venue since its opening and operates as a national cultural center. The judge's decision emphasizes the facility's historical designation and its status as a living memorial to the late president.

cards.headline: Trump says decision on Iran deal coming soon, demands Hormuz Strait reopening
cards.teaser: President Trump held a Situation Room meeting on Iran but did not announce a final determination on a proposed deal.
cards.body:
President Trump convened advisers in the Situation Room to discuss Iran negotiations after the U.S. and Iran agreed on a deal framework. Trump deferred announcing a final decision following the meeting.

Trump stated he will soon determine whether to accept the Iran proposal and called for the Strait of Hormuz to be reopened. Recent military strikes between the two countries have complicated ongoing negotiations.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran cease-fire extension
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers for two hours at the White House about a possible extension.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his advisers for two hours at the White House to discuss a potential Iran cease-fire extension. The meeting came after Trump had indicated on social media that he was prepared to announce a decision on the matter.

U.S. and Iranian officials have confirmed they reached agreement on a framework for a deal. The discussions centered on extending an existing cease-fire arrangement between the two countries.

cards.headline: Ukraine braces for major Russian attacks in next 24 hours
cards.teaser: President Zelenskyy said Russia is preparing a significant new offensive.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warned that Russia is preparing a major new attack on Ukraine within the next 24 hours. The warning prompted an emergency meeting of the Security Council on Ukraine and a live session at the United Nations.

The alert comes as Russia intensifies its assault on Ukraine. A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania during an overnight attack, injuring two people. Russian officials have warned Europe to expect more such incidents.

cards.headline: Russian drone hits apartment building in Romania, injuring civilians
cards.body:
A Russian drone struck a residential building in the eastern Romanian city of Galati during an overnight attack on Ukraine, injuring two people and sparking a fire. The incident marked the first time civilians were wounded by a cross-border drone strike in the NATO member country.

The drone crashed into the roof of the apartment building on Friday, forcing the evacuation of several residents. Romanian military forces scrambled two F-16 fighter jets and a helicopter in response, while emergency services treated the injured and issued alerts to residents in affected areas.

The strike prompted immediate diplomatic responses from NATO and European leaders. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance is "ready to defend every inch" of its territory after speaking with Romanian President Nicusor Dan. "Russia's reckless behaviour is a danger to us all," Rutte stated.

Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu said her country would formally communicate consequences to Russia and consider diplomatic repercussions. The foreign ministry described the incident as a "grave and irresponsible escalation" and a serious breach of international law. Romania's government announced it would request NATO to accelerate the transfer of anti-drone capabilities and suggested invoking Article 4 of the NATO treaty, which triggers formal discussions within the alliance about security threats.

Romanian President Dan convened an emergency meeting of the country's supreme council of national defence and instructed the foreign ministry to prepare a package of measures regarding Romania's relationship with Moscow. He said Romania would not accept the war being transferred to its citizens.

Russia denied responsibility for the strike. Vladimir Putin suggested without evidence that the drone might have been a stray Ukrainian weapon and called for the wreckage to be handed over for independent investigation. A Romanian military commander stated the strike was not "an attack from Russia against Romania," but emphasized that Russians should understand Russia poses a threat to regional security.

Galati is located on the Danube River, west of Romania's borders with Moldova and Ukraine. Romanian authorities said the drone was tracked by radar in Romanian airspace before impact.

International leaders swiftly condemned the incident. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyer said Russia's "war of aggression has crossed yet another line," while French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot denounced what he called an irresponsible act. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the incident demonstrated Russia poses a threat to all of Europe.

The strike represents a significant escalation in how the Ukraine conflict affects neighboring countries. Drones from the war have previously entered Romanian airspace, but this marked the first occasion resulting in civilian injuries. The incident occurs amid broader concerns about Russian hybrid warfare operations across Europe.

cards.headline: UN adds Israel and Russia to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations placed both countries on its list for conflict-related sexual violence.
cards.body:
The United Nations has added Israel and Russia to its blacklist for sexual violence in armed conflict. The UN verified sexual abuse of 31 Palestinian men, women and children from Gaza and the occupied West Bank between 2023 and 2025. According to the report, Israeli security forces committed repeated gang-rapes and used sexual violence as a form of torture.

Russia was also placed on the blacklist for sexual violence committed during armed conflict, including the rape of male detainees. Both governments have blocked UN investigators from accessing their territories, hampering independent verification efforts.

cards.headline: Ghana parliament passes bill criminalizing LGBTQ promotion
cards.teaser: Lawmakers approved legislation that would criminalize the promotion of LGBTQ activities.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament approved a bill criminalizing the promotion of LGBTQ activities, an official said. The legislation now awaits the president's signature.

The bill would criminalize LGBTQ people and activities in the country. However, one lawmaker insisted that no anti-LGBTQ bill was presented to President Akufo-Addo, creating confusion about the status of the legislation.

cards.headline: Canadian man pleads guilty to aiding 14 suicides
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law ran an online business that shipped toxic salt to customers in 40 countries.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide in Canada after prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges. The Canadian man mailed toxic chemicals to more than 100 people across dozens of countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia and New Zealand, often with instructions on how to use them.

Law appeared in court in Newmarket, Ontario, to enter his plea. Families of 79 British victims have called for him to be charged in the UK as well. Sentencing is expected in September.

cards.headline: First of five men rescued from flooded Laos cave
cards.teaser: One man was led to safety after nine days stranded in the cavern.
cards.body:
The first of seven men trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for more than a week has been rescued by divers in a perilous operation. The man was brought to safety after being stranded in the remote cavern.

Four of the men remain inside a chamber about 300 metres from the cave entrance, where they were found huddled together on a rocky ledge. Two men are still missing. The rescue required teams to navigate narrow, water-filled tunnels with sharp rocks and collapse hazards. An international team of divers, including some who participated in the 2018 Thai cave rescue, has been deployed to extract the remaining survivors.

cards.headline: Judge temporarily halts payouts from Trump's $1.776 billion settlement fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge blocked the Trump administration from making immediate payments from an anti-weaponization settlement fund.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into a $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema issued the order on Friday, barring the government from taking further action in creating or operating the fund while legal challenges proceed.

The order aims to prevent funds from being irreversibly disbursed while the case challenging the fund continues. The secretive and loosely controlled settlement fund is now frozen pending the resolution of ongoing legal arguments.

cards.teaser: President Trump held a Situation Room meeting on Iran but did not announce a final determination on a proposed deal.

President Trump convened advisers in the Situation Room to discuss Iran negotiations after the U.S. and Iran agreed on a deal framework. Trump deferred announcing a final decision following the meeting.

Trump stated he will soon determine whether to accept the Iran proposal and called for the Strait of Hormuz to be reopened. Recent military strikes between the two countries have complicated ongoing negotiations.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks U.S. plan to treat American Ebola patients in Africa
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court suspended plans for a U.S. quarantine facility in the country for American Ebola patients.
cards.body:
A court in Kenya blocked a U.S. plan to establish a quarantine facility in the country for treating American Ebola patients. The suspension of the proposed facility meant infected Americans would not receive treatment in Kenya as originally planned.

Following the court's decision, U.S. officials announced that Americans who contract Ebola will instead receive treatment in Europe. The proposed facility had faced opposition from both Kenyan and American critics.

cards.headline: Bus crash on I-95 in Virginia kills five, injures dozens
cards.teaser: Police identified the driver in a Virginia bus crash that killed five people, including two children, and injured more than 40.
cards.body:
Five people died and more than 40 were injured after a bus crashed on Interstate 95 southbound in Stafford County, Virginia. Police identified the driver following the incident. The victims included a 13-year-old, a 7-year-old, and three adults.

A survivor described the bus as going really fast before the crash. The incident caused a massive pileup on the interstate.

cards.headline: Attorney General Bondi assigns Epstein files responsibility to Todd Blanche
cards.teaser: Attorney General Pam Bondi told lawmakers that redaction errors were made in the Epstein files release and shifted oversight to Todd Blanche.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before the House Oversight and Reform Committee about the Department of Justice's handling of Jeffrey Epstein files. Bondi acknowledged that redaction errors occurred during the release but defended the overall process, stating she did not personally lead every aspect of the effort.

Bondi delegated oversight of the Epstein files release to Todd Blanche, her former deputy attorney general who is now serving as acting attorney general. Democratic lawmakers pressed Bondi on questions about Donald Trump's involvement in the files' release, which she declined to answer.

cards.headline: Three climbers dead, one rescued after fall on Alaska's Mount McKinley
cards.teaser: Three climbers died after falling near a treacherous pass on Mount McKinley in Alaska, while one was rescued.
cards.body:
Three climbers died after falling near a treacherous pass on Alaska's Mount McKinley. One climber was rescued from the incident.

Rescue operations recovered the bodies of the three deceased climbers from the dangerous section of the mountain.

hero.headline: Stock markets close at record highs as tech leads May rally
hero.body:
Wall Street finished Friday at new highs, concluding a strong month driven by technology stocks and growing investor confidence about potential diplomatic progress in the Middle East. The Nasdaq advanced 8% during May, marking one of its most impressive monthly gains in recent years.

Technology companies spearheaded the market advance as investors bet on continued expansion in artificial intelligence and connected sectors. The gains extended a broader rally that has pushed major indexes to repeated records throughout the month.

Market sentiment also received support from reports suggesting the United States and Iran are moving closer to an agreement that could extend a cease-fire. This potential diplomatic breakthrough helped boost risk appetite across financial markets.

Oil prices moved in the opposite direction, heading toward their largest monthly decline since 2020. The drop in crude reflected expectations that reduced tensions in the Middle East could ease supply concerns that had supported energy markets earlier in the year.

The combination of falling oil prices and rising stock values indicated investors believe lower energy costs could sustain economic growth without triggering inflation. Strong corporate profit reports have provided fundamental backing for higher stock valuations.

All three major U.S. stock indexes posted gains for both the session and the month. The rally continued the market strength that has characterized much of 2026, with technology shares playing an outsized role in propelling returns.

However, this technology-focused strength stands in contrast to broader market trends. A rotation away from expensive artificial intelligence and growth stocks toward businesses with tangible infrastructure has gained momentum. Investors have increasingly moved into energy, materials, industrials and other traditional sectors offering what analysts call "heavy assets and low obsolescence" - companies with substantial physical capital less vulnerable to disruption.

The FTSE 100 in London, which contains many established economy companies, has hit multiple record highs in 2026. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index also reached record levels recently, benefiting from this rotation out of U.S. technology stocks into other sectors.

In contrast to the tech rally in the U.S., software and data-focused companies have faced recent pressure as artificial intelligence services threaten their business models. Markets were also rattled last week by a speculative report outlining potential scenarios where autonomous AI systems could upend the economy.

Investors are watching for further developments in U.S.-Iran negotiations, which could influence both energy markets and broader risk sentiment in coming sessions. Market participants are also awaiting policy decisions from the Trump administration on Middle East issues that could reshape the diplomatic landscape.

The May gains arrived despite earlier concerns about economic headwinds and geopolitical tensions. Strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm about technological innovation have outweighed worries about interest rates and global trade dynamics.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall toward largest monthly drop since 2020
cards.teaser: Crude prices declined as investors assessed signs of progress toward extending a Middle East cease-fire.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell sharply as investors grew optimistic about a potential agreement between the United States and Iran to extend a cease-fire. Brent crude futures, the global benchmark, dropped 1.3% on Friday to around $92 per barrel.

The monthly decline has been substantial, with Brent crude down 19% since the end of April, marking the steepest monthly fall since 2020. Stock markets rallied alongside the oil price decline, as investors viewed cheaper energy costs as potentially beneficial for economic growth.

cards.headline: Universal Music rejects billionaire Bill Ackman's takeover offer
cards.teaser: The music company said Pershing Square's proposal fundamentally undervalued the business.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group rejected a takeover bid from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's firm Pershing Square. The proposed offer valued the music company at approximately $64 billion to $65 billion, but Universal's board determined it fundamentally undervalued the business.

The rejection marks a significant setback for Ackman's attempt to acquire one of the world's largest music companies.

cards.headline: UnitedHealthcare drops prior approval requirements for most pediatric services
cards.teaser: The insurer will eliminate authorization requirements for nearly two-thirds of pediatric medical services.
cards.body:
UnitedHealthcare announced it will remove prior insurance approval requirements for a majority of pediatric services. The change affects nearly two-thirds of medical services for children, eliminating a step that often delayed care.

Prior authorization has been a source of friction between insurers, doctors and patients. The requirements forced healthcare providers to obtain approval from insurance companies before delivering certain treatments. UnitedHealthcare's decision reduces administrative barriers for pediatric care.

cards.headline: Trump administration clears tax avoidance schemes in Malta and Cyprus
cards.teaser: U.S. companies avoided at least $40 billion in taxes since early 2025 using structures in tax havens.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has allowed U.S. companies to avoid taxes through schemes based in jurisdictions including Malta, Bermuda and Cyprus. American corporations have skirted at least $40 billion in tax obligations since the beginning of 2025 using these structures.

The arrangements take advantage of favorable tax treatment in certain foreign jurisdictions. Companies route profits through these locations to reduce their U.S. tax bills. The administration's approach represents a policy choice about how aggressively to pursue tax avoidance strategies.

cards.headline: Wall Street banks prepare for massive SpaceX public offering
cards.teaser: Elon Musk and bankers are working to convince investors the risks of missing the deal outweigh concerns about buying in.
cards.body:
Elon Musk and Wall Street banks are orchestrating a strategy to build momentum for SpaceX's upcoming public offering. They aim to create a self-fulfilling prophecy by generating investor enthusiasm around the deal, making the opportunity feel too significant to miss.

The approach focuses on convincing investors that the risks of sitting out the offering outweigh those of participating. By cultivating strong demand ahead of the stock sale, the banks and Musk hope to ensure the offering's success. The planned IPO would rank among the largest public debuts in recent years.

cards.headline: NextEra Energy's political influence in Florida examined amid Dominion deal
cards.teaser: The utility company has clashed with consumer advocates and residents while pursuing the acquisition.
cards.body:
NextEra Energy has wielded significant political power in Florida as it seeks approval to acquire Dominion Energy. The utility company has frequently been at odds with consumer groups, residents and journalists in its home state.

NextEra's political activities have drawn scrutiny as regulators consider the Dominion purchase. The company's approach to navigating Florida politics could influence how stakeholders view the proposed transaction. The acquisition would expand NextEra's footprint in the energy sector.

hero.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to relocate Americans exposed to Ebola
hero.body:
A Kenyan court blocked the Trump administration from relocating Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya. The decision prevents the US government from transferring individuals who may have been exposed to the virus to facilities in the African nation.

The United States has previously constructed specialized medical facilities designed specifically for handling individuals exposed to highly infectious diseases like Ebola. These facilities were built to isolate and treat potential Ebola patients on US soil.

The court ruling comes as the US explored alternative locations for quarantine and treatment of Americans who encountered Ebola exposure. Kenya emerged as a potential destination for such relocations under the current administration's plans.

The decision by Kenyan judges represents a setback for US contingency planning around infectious disease management. The ruling suggests that international cooperation on public health emergencies cannot proceed without host country approval, even when involving American citizens.

The existence of purpose-built Ebola treatment facilities in the United States raises questions about why the administration sought to relocate exposed individuals abroad. These specialized centers were constructed with advanced isolation capabilities and medical equipment tailored to handling hemorrhagic fever cases.

Ebola virus disease is a severe illness with high fatality rates that spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected individuals. The virus has caused multiple outbreaks in Africa over the past decades, prompting international health agencies to develop strict protocols for managing exposure cases.

The Trump administration has not publicly explained the rationale behind seeking to transfer potentially exposed Americans to Kenya rather than using domestic facilities. The Kenyan government's position on the proposal before the court intervention also remains unclear from available information.

cards.headline: SpaceX secures $6.45 billion in Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The company disclosed that government work already accounts for 20 percent of its revenue.
cards.body:
SpaceX secured $6.45 billion in contracts from the Space Force, according to documents filed for the company's initial public offering. The aerospace manufacturer disclosed the award as it prepares to become a publicly traded company.

The IPO filing reveals that government contracts accounted for one-fifth of SpaceX's total revenue in 2025. These Space Force awards underscore the company's significant role as a defense contractor supporting military and government space operations.

cards.headline: FCC warns broadcasters of punishment following ABC case
cards.teaser: ABC said the early renewal terms for all its stations have no precedent or legitimate purpose.
cards.body:
The Federal Communications Commission under the Trump administration issued a warning to all broadcasters that they must follow orders or face consequences similar to those imposed on ABC. The commission's statement followed action taken against the network.

ABC responded that the FCC's requirement for early renewal of all its broadcast stations is unprecedented in regulatory history. The network said the mandate serves no legitimate purpose under existing communications law.

cards.headline: Law enforcement dismantles botnet controlling 17 million devices
cards.teaser: The network was linked to a Russia-based residential proxy service.
cards.body:
Authorities dismantled a botnet that had compromised more than 17 million devices worldwide. The operation targeted one of the largest known networks of infected computers and connected devices.

Investigators tied the botnet to a residential proxy network operating from Russia. These proxy services route internet traffic through infected home devices to mask the true origin of online activities.

cards.headline: Texas measles outbreak analysis shows high hospitalization rate
cards.teaser: About 20 percent of cases required hospital care, with most developing complications.
cards.body:
An analysis of a measles outbreak in Texas found that approximately one in five infected individuals required hospitalization. Most of those hospitalized developed medical complications from the virus.

Measles is a highly contagious viral disease that can lead to serious complications including pneumonia, brain swelling, and death, particularly in young children and immunocompromised individuals.

---

Note: The source material provided is about an Ebola outbreak in the DRC, not the Texas measles outbreak. Since it covers a different story, I've returned the original card text unchanged as instructed.

cards.headline: Justice Department sues states over ICE license plate denials
cards.teaser: The DOJ accused monitoring sites of revealing agent identities, though evidence remains limited.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice filed lawsuits against states that rejected requests from Immigration and Customs Enforcement for undercover license plates. The legal action targets state motor vehicle agencies that declined to issue the specialized plates to ICE agents.

The Justice Department has repeatedly accused websites that monitor ICE activity of revealing agent identities, characterizing this as doxing. However, concrete evidence supporting these accusations remains scarce in public filings and statements.

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI coding tools may reduce code quality
cards.teaser: Programmers increasingly refuse to work without AI assistance despite quality concerns.
cards.body:
Software developers are increasingly refusing to work without artificial intelligence coding assistants, even as researchers warn the tools may not improve code quality. The trend shows growing dependence on AI in software development.

While AI helps programmers write code faster, researchers caution it may not produce better code. This quality gap could create problems for developers and their projects in the future as AI-generated code accumulates in software systems.

hero.headline: Novak Djokovic loses to Joao Fonseca in French Open third round
hero.body:
Novak Djokovic's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title ended at the French Open after a five-set loss to 19-year-old Brazilian Joao Fonseca in the third round at Roland Garros.

The defeat marks a significant upset for the tennis legend, who fell to the teenage opponent in what multiple outlets described as a historic loss. Fonseca, competing in his first French Open, defeated Djokovic over five sets in a match that extended the tournament's trend of top seeds falling early.

The loss means Roland Garros will crown a first-time major champion this year, the first time that has happened at the tournament in years. Djokovic had been among the favorites entering the clay court Grand Slam, but joined other top players in exiting earlier than expected.

Fonseca's victory over one of tennis's all-time greats signals his arrival among the sport's elite players. The 19-year-old Brazilian had been rising through professional tennis ranks but had not previously defeated a player of Djokovic's caliber in a Grand Slam setting.

Djokovic, who has won 24 Grand Slam singles titles, was seeking to extend his record with a 25th major championship. The Serbian player has dominated men's tennis for over a decade alongside rivals Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal, collecting titles across all four major tournaments.

The French Open, played on clay courts at Roland Garros in Paris, is one of tennis's four Grand Slam tournaments. Djokovic has won the French Open three times previously, though clay has historically been his least successful Grand Slam surface compared to hard courts and grass.

With Djokovic's elimination, the men's draw opens up significantly for the remaining players. The tournament will continue through its quarterfinal and semifinal rounds before crowning a champion who will be winning their first major title.

Fonseca will advance to the fourth round, where he will face another opponent as he continues his unexpected run through the draw at his first appearance in the main draw of the French Open.

cards.headline: Nationals executive removed after video shows comments about avoiding conservative player
cards.teaser: A Washington Nationals executive was let go after a video surfaced showing him saying the team avoided using a conservative player on social media.
cards.body:
The Washington Nationals dismissed an executive after video footage showed the official saying the team deliberately avoided featuring a conservative player in its social media content. The recording was obtained by The New York Times.

The executive's remarks drew attention to a Catholic pitcher, prompting a Catholic advocacy group to call for a Department of Justice investigation into potential religious discrimination by the organization.

cards.headline: Giants linebacker Abdul Carter calls out teammate Jaxson Dart over Trump introduction
cards.teaser: New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter publicly called out quarterback Jaxson Dart to demonstrate his opposition to Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Giants linebacker Abdul Carter publicly addressed teammate Jaxson Dart after the quarterback introduced President Trump at a rally. The disagreement prompted a team meeting where Dart explained his decision to his teammates.

Following their initial clash, both players expressed unity, according to ESPN. Giants coach John Harbaugh was expected to address the situation but was unlikely to criticize Dart's appearance at the Trump event.

cards.headline: MLB suspends Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for gesture toward Cardinals
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball suspended Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for one game following actions during a game against the St. Louis Cardinals.
cards.body:
Abner Uribe received a one-game suspension from MLB for performing what the league deemed an inappropriate gesture during the Brewers' win over the Cardinals. The suspension was issued for a DX Chop celebration that Uribe made on video during the game.

Uribe has appealed the suspension, according to ESPN and MLB.com. The gesture occurred during Milwaukee's victory against St. Louis, leading to the league's disciplinary action against the relief pitcher.

cards.headline: Steelers fire assistant special teams coach Derius Swinton II after three months
cards.teaser: The Pittsburgh Steelers dismissed assistant special teams coach Derius Swinton II just months into his tenure with the team.
cards.body:
Derius Swinton II was fired from his position as senior assistant special teams coach with the Steelers after approximately three months on the job. According to NFL.com and NBC Sports, the dismissal was due to a violation of club policy.

The Steelers parted ways with Swinton after a brief period with the organization, though the specific nature of the policy violation was not detailed in reports. The sudden dismissal came as Swinton was still in the early stages of his role with the coaching staff.

cards.headline: Sacramento unveils MLB expansion ballpark plans and funding
cards.teaser: Sacramento officially presented its proposal for an MLB expansion team, including ballpark details and funding structure.
cards.body:
The California capital city released its formal bid to secure a Major League Baseball expansion franchise, complete with stadium plans and financial backing. Sacramento becomes another Western city pursuing MLB expansion, joining ongoing discussions about adding teams to the league.

Investors backing the Sacramento proposal include several prominent names, according to the Sacramento Bee. Local fans expressed readiness for a major league team, with KCRA reporting strong community support for bringing professional baseball to the region.

cards.headline: Golfer Ian Poulter requires knee surgery after tearing meniscus
cards.teaser: British golfer Ian Poulter needs surgery after injuring his knee at a LIV Golf event in Virginia.
cards.body:
British golfer Ian Poulter sustained a torn meniscus while hopping up two steps at a LIV Golf event in Virginia earlier this month. The injury, occurring during a routine movement, has forced him to undergo surgery.

Poulter announced that he will require a surgical procedure to repair the damage to his knee before he can return to professional competition.

hero.headline: Over Half of Great American State Fair Performers Drop Out
hero.body:
More than half of the scheduled performers for the Great American State Fair have withdrawn from the event, citing politics and threats. The concert, also known as the US Freedom 250 or Freedom 250 concert, is backed by President Donald Trump and planned for this summer as part of America's 250th anniversary celebrations.

Vanilla Ice remains the last confirmed act on the lineup after multiple artists withdrew. The departures have left the event with a significantly reduced roster of performers compared to initial plans.

The withdrawals come amid reported concerns from artists about the political nature of the event and threats they received. The concert was intended as a major celebration tied to the nation's semicentennial, but the wave of cancellations has put the programming in question.

Organizers have not announced replacement performers or changes to the event schedule. The Great American State Fair was positioned as a marquee entertainment component of the 250th anniversary observances, but the roster now consists of a single confirmed headliner.

The event's connection to Trump and its political framing appear to have driven artists' decisions to pull out. Multiple news outlets reported that performers cited both the political associations and security concerns related to threats as reasons for their departures.

The scale of the cancellations represents a significant setback for the event. With only Vanilla Ice confirmed, organizers face the challenge of either recruiting new talent or potentially reconsidering the scope of the concert.

The 250th anniversary of American independence falls in 2026, and various commemorative events have been planned across the country. The Great American State Fair was intended to be among the highest-profile entertainment offerings, but the performer exodus has complicated those plans.

Neither the event organizers nor representatives for the departing artists have provided detailed public statements about the specific threats or political concerns that prompted the mass withdrawal.

cards.headline: Trump Says Judge Should Be Ashamed Over Kennedy Center Ruling
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump criticized a judge who halted renovations at the Kennedy Center and ordered his name removed from the building.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered that Trump's name be removed from the Kennedy Center and blocked planned renovations to the performing arts venue. The judge's 94-page ruling stated it was "crystal clear" that the center was named after President John F. Kennedy.

Trump responded by saying the judge should be ashamed of himself. The ruling also prevents the Kennedy Center from closing for the two-year renovation period Trump had announced. Following the decision, Trump said he would transfer control of the institution to Congress.

cards.headline: Maddox Jolie-Pitt Drops Father's Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox, the eldest son of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt, is legally removing Pitt from his surname.
cards.body:
Maddox Jolie-Pitt, 24, has legally removed his father's last name. He is the fourth of Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt's children to take this action.

Brad Pitt has reportedly been hurt by the decision. According to sources, he has limited ability to influence his adult children's choices regarding their surnames as they continue to side with their mother following the family's separation.

cards.headline: Kanye West Approved to Perform in Netherlands
cards.teaser: Officials cleared Kanye West to enter the Netherlands for a performance on his birthday.
cards.body:
Dutch officials ruled that insufficient evidence exists to ban rapper Kanye West from entering the country. The decision allows West to perform in the Netherlands on his birthday.

The ruling came after officials reviewed the case. West had faced the possibility of being barred from entry, but authorities determined there was not enough justification for a ban.

cards.headline: Defamation Judgment Against Blogger Reinstated in Megan Thee Stallion Case
cards.teaser: A judge reinstated a defamation judgment against blogger Milagro Gramz in a case involving Megan Thee Stallion.
cards.body:
A judge found that blogger Milagro Gramz was commissioned by Tory Lanez's family to brand Megan Thee Stallion a liar. The finding stripped Gramz of media defendant protections for those statements.

The ruling reinstated the defamation judgment against Gramz. The judge determined that her actions went beyond typical journalism because she was acting on behalf of Lanez's family in making the statements about Megan Thee Stallion.

cards.headline: Hannah Einbinder Opposes Spencer Pratt's LA Mayoral Run
cards.teaser: The Hacks star spoke out against Spencer Pratt's campaign to become Los Angeles mayor.
cards.body:
Hannah Einbinder said it is important to resist Spencer Pratt's mayoral campaign for Los Angeles. She made the comments following the emotional series finale of Hacks.

Einbinder said there is a lot of wealth in the city and many people present themselves as Democrats or leftists but prioritize money as their key issue. She suggested Pratt's campaign represents these priorities.

cards.headline: Becky G and Santana Release Song About ICE Raids
cards.teaser: The artists released a song depicting the realities of immigration enforcement operations.
cards.body:
Becky G and Santana released Mi Gran Amor, a song that portrays the harsh realities of ICE raids. Becky G told Rolling Stone there is power in using music to humanize conversations.

The track addresses immigration enforcement through a musical lens. The collaboration between Becky G and Santana aims to bring human stories to the forefront of discussions about immigration policy.

hero.headline: Pentagon's $9 billion Dell contract raises conflict of interest questions
hero.teaser: The Department of Defense announced a five-year agreement with Dell after President Trump promoted the company and bought its stock.
hero.body:
The Pentagon awarded a $9.7 billion contract to Dell this week for Microsoft software and cloud services. The Department of Defense announced the five-year agreement as part of an effort to consolidate technology services.

The deal raised questions about potential conflicts of interest. President Trump previously promoted Dell's products and purchased significant amounts of the company's stock before the contract was awarded.

cards.headline: Detention facility becomes first major test for new DHS secretary
cards.teaser: Protesters have been arrested outside Delaney Hall while detainees reportedly participate in a hunger strike.
cards.body:
A private detention center in New Jersey has become a flashpoint in the fight over the Trump administration's immigration policies. The situation marks the first major test for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

Protesters have been arrested outside the Delaney Hall Facility while detainees reportedly take part in a hunger strike. Detainees have made claims of inhumane living conditions and inadequate medical care. The 1,000-bed facility in Newark reopened last year and has been the scene of escalating tensions since then.

cards.headline: Bulgaria to end US military aircraft stay over visa dispute
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the aircraft stay in Sofia will end after the Trump administration did not approve visa-free travel.
cards.body:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev announced Friday that the country will terminate the deployment of U.S. military aircraft in Sofia by the end of June. The decision stems from the Trump administration's refusal to approve visa-free travel for Bulgarian citizens to the United States.

Radev had requested the suspension of visas for Bulgarian visitors during discussions with U.S. officials. The withdrawal will affect the American military aircraft currently stationed in the Bulgarian capital.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary endorses $250 bill featuring President Trump
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent supported the proposed currency during an interview at the Ronald Reagan Presidential Library.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent endorsed a proposed $250 bill featuring President Trump to commemorate the U.S. semiquincentennial, the country's 250th anniversary of independence. Bessent announced the proposal at a White House news conference, stating that the treasury department has already begun preparing for the possibility of printing the new currency.

The proposal would require changing federal law, which currently prohibits any living person from appearing on U.S. currency. Trump allies in Congress are working to make an exception for this commemorative bill, while Democrats have vowed to block the move.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor creates protected protest zones at detention facility
cards.teaser: Governor Sherrill announced plans for designated areas at Delaney Hall amid escalating tensions.
cards.body:
New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and Attorney General Jennifer Davenport announced that state police will take over policing operations at the Delaney Hall detention facility from federal immigration officers. The move comes as federal agents have increased their presence at the site.

As part of the transition, state police will establish a "peaceful protected zone" for demonstrators at the facility, where protesters are expected to gather. The announcement follows reports of a hunger strike by detainees and recent protest activity at the Newark location.

cards.headline: Former Iowa schools chief sentenced to two years on immigration and gun charges
cards.teaser: Ian Roberts pleaded guilty to falsely claiming citizenship and illegally possessing a firearm.
cards.body:
Ian Roberts, the former superintendent of Des Moines schools, was sentenced Friday to two years in prison after pleading guilty to federal charges of falsely claiming to be a U.S. citizen and illegally possessing a firearm.

Roberts led one of Iowa's largest school districts, serving more than 30,000 students, from 2023 until his arrest.

cards.headline: Jill Biden calls husband's cancer diagnosis shocking
cards.teaser: The former first lady said the prostate cancer diagnosis was missed during routine screening.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden described her husband's cancer diagnosis as shocking in a new interview with CBS News. In a preview clip released from the interview with Rita Braver, Biden said the diagnosis was somehow missed during earlier medical evaluations.

Former President Biden revealed his prostate cancer diagnosis in May of last year. A spokesperson confirmed the diagnosis at that time.
